title: Finland – Gravel, sand, crushed stone and aggregates – Kivi- ja maa-aineksen puitesopimus
description: Puolustusvoimien logistiikkalaitos (jäljempänä Hankintayksikkö) pyytää tarjoustanne Kivi- ja maa-aineksen toimituksista Uudenmaan prikaatin ja Panssariprikaatin tarpeisiin, tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Kummankin joukko-osaston tarpeeseen valitaan yksi tai kaksi toimittajaa ja valittujen toimittajien kanssa tehdään puitesopimus joukko-osaston (jäljempänä tilaaja) käyttöön. Tarjouspyynnön kivi- ja maa-ainesten määrät ovat arvioituja yhteenlaskettuja määriä koko sopimuskaudelle, sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta neljän (4) vuoden ajaksi ja ne voivat sopimuksen aikana ylittyä tai alittua arvioidusta. Tilattavan aineksen todellista määrää ei pystytä kertomaan tarkemmin, koska alueiden kunnostustyöt riippuvat siihen myönnetyistä määrärahoista ja alueiden käytöstä. Tilaajan yhteyshenkilöt tilaavat tarpeen ilmaantuessa erillisten tilausten perusteella sopimuksen mukaisia tuotteita valituilta toimittajilta.

title: Finland – Domestic appliances – Espoon Asunnot Oy / Kodinkoneiden toimitus, -asennus ja -huolto puitesopimus 2027
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Kodinkoneiden toimitus, -asennus ja -huolto palvelujen tuottaminen Espoon Asunnot Oy:n omistamissa kiinteistöissä. Palvelu sisältää mm.: • Kodinkoneiden tarkastus-, korjaus ja huoltopalvelut • Kodinkoneiden toimituspalvelut • Kodinkoneiden asennuspalvelut • seuranta, raportointi ja dokumentointi • neuvonta tilaajille ja asukkaille Palvelu tuotetaan tilausten perusteella tilaajan kiinteistöissä. Valinta Hankinta jaetaan pääsääntöisesti maantieteellisiin osiin. Hankintayksikkö tekee toimittajan puitesopimus, johon valitaan kaksi palveluntuottajaa. Sopimus tulisi olemaan kestoltaan 4 vuotta. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen maantieteelliseen alueeseen sekä uudiskohteiden laitteisiin ilman asennusta. Kahdelle alueelle valitaan kumppani hoitamaan kodinkoneiden toimitukset ja huolto. Kilpailutuksessa seuraavaksi halvimman molempia alueita tarjonnut valitaan varasijalle, jonka kanssa voidaan tehdä sopimus, jos jomman kumman valitun kanssa ei sopimukseen päästä tai sopimus päätetään kesken sopimuksen. Halvempi tarjoaja saa valita eteläinen vai pohjoinen alue. Uudis- ja peruskorjauskohteet eivät välttämättä noudata samaa aluejakoa. Vaihtoehdot sopimuksen toteuttamisessa ovat seuraavat: 1. Tarjouksen antava yritys voi itse hoitaa sekä kodinkoneiden toimituksen että huollon. 2. Tarjouksen antava yritys toimii kodinkoneiden toimittajana ja yrityksen alihankkija tekee kodinkoneiden huollot. Koko palvelu on kuitenkin tarjottava yhtenä sopimuksena ja kaikki palvelut laskutettava saman toimittajan toimesta Hankinnan kohteena on Espoon Asunnot Oy:n kodinkoneiden toimitukset, -huolto ja -asennuspalvelut. Tilaajalla on tarve molemmilla alueilla noin 1500 kodinkoneen uusimiselle ja 1000 uudelle kodinkoneelle sekä noin 3000 huolto-/asennuskäyntiä per vuosi. Tilaaja ei voi kertoa tarkkoja määriä ennalta eikä luvata tiettyä määrää töitä tai laitteita sopimusaikana. Hintalistan määräarviot ovat ainoastaan tarjousten vertailua varten. Hankinta jaetaan kahteen osaan: Osa 1: Etelä Osa 2: Pohjoinen Hinnoitellaan erikseen: Uudis- ja peruskorjauskohteen kodinkoneet Uudis ja peruskorjauskohteissa lähtökohtaisesti noudatetaan samaa aluejakoa. Kaikkia alueita tarjotaan samalla tarjouksella. Tilaaja valitsee yhteensä 2 sopimuskumppania. Tarjoaja voi käyttää sopimuksen toteuttamisessa myös alihankkijaa eli tarjoaja voi - hoitaa kodinkoneiden toimituksen, -asennus ja huoltopalvelut itse - hoitaa kodinkoneiden toimituksen ja yrityksen alihankkija hoitaa kuljetus-, asennus- ja huoltopalvelut. Tilaaja kuitenkin asioi vain sopimuskumppanin kautta ja vain sopimuskumppani laskuttaa tilaajaa yhdellä laskulla per tilaus. Toimittaja valitaan halvimpien vertailuhintojen perusteella Tarjouksen hintalomakkeessa tulee ilmoittaa arvonlisäverolliset hinnat työselostuksessa kuvattujen työsisältöjen perusteella. description: Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos pyytää tarjousta Jäänhoito- ja latukoneiden huolto- ja korjauspalveluista sopimuskaudelle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2027. Mahdolliset optiokaudet vuosi kerrallaan ajanjaksolle 1.1.2028 - 31.12.2030. Tilaaja ilmoittaa optioiden luopumisesta 3kk ennen optiokauden alkamista, muutoin optiot tulevat käyttöön ja voimaan automaattisesti. Hankinnasta perustetaan puitejärjestely. Osa-alueen etusijajärjestys määräytyy vertailun kokonaispistemäärän perusteella. Eniten pisteitä saanut tarjoaja sijoittuu ensimmäiseksi. Huoltopalvelun osa-alueilla vertailuperusteena on hinta. Akuuttikorjauksen osa-alueilla vertailuperusteina ovat hinta 95 pistettä ja samaa laitemerkkiä koskevan huoltopalvelun tarjoaminen 5 pistettä. Palveluntuottajia valitaan enintään kaksi per osa-alue. Varsinainen palveluntuottaja ja varasijalle toinen. Mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia saadaan vain yksi, tilaaja voi perustaa puitejärjestelyn kyseiseen osa-alueeseen yhden toimittajan kanssa. Kaikkia osa-alueita (kaikki jäänhoitokonemerkit) ei tarvitse tarjota. Tuntihintojen ja pisteytyskriteerien tarjoaminen tapahtuu "hankinnat kohdan kriteerit" kohdassa. Huolto- ja tuntihinnat tarjotaan per laitemerkki erikseen. Lisäpisteitä saa, jos samaan merkkiin tarjotaan sekä huolto- että korjauspalvelua. Tällöin korjauspalvelun kohdalla tulee merkitä ”kyllä” tarjottu huoltopalvelua. Tarjottuun hinta on esitettävä arvonlisäverottomina (alv 0 %) nettohintoina, jotka sisältävät kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta aiheutuvat kustannukset mahdolliset kilometri, matka-, majoitus-, päiväraha-, ylityö- sekä toimitus-, laskutus- ja toimistokulut mukaan lukien. Matka-ajasta saa laskuttaa tarjouslomakkeella ilmoitettua tuntihintaa enintään yhdeltä henkilöltä. Matka-aika lasketaan lyhintä tavanomaista ajoreittiä pitkin Oulun kaupungin hallinnolliselta rajalta tai toimittajan Oulun kaupungin alueella sijaitsevasta vakituisesta toimipisteestä työkohteeseen ja takaisin. Erillisiä kilometri-, päiväraha-, majoitus- tai muita matkakuluja ei saa laskuttaa. Mikäli 1. sijoittunut ei pysty /on estynyt ottamasta työtä vastaan, tilaaja käyttää 2. sijoittunutta palveluntarjoajaa. Valittu palveluntuottaja ei voi ilman perusteltua syytä kieltäytyä vastaanottamasta työtilausta ja perustelut annetaan kirjallisesti esim. sähköpostin välityksellä. Huoltopalvelun ja ei-kiireellisen korjauksen vasteaika arkisin on 5 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Akuuttikorjauspalvelun vasteaika arkisin ja viikonloppuisin on 1 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Töitä saavat tilata ainoastaan tilaajan nimeämät yhteyshenkilöt (työnjohtajat), jotka määrittelee erikseen työtä tilatessaan, onko työ huolto- vai ei-kiireellistä tai akuuttikorjaustyötä. Huoltopalvelu suoritetaan merkkivalmistajan huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti ja tarjoajalla tulee olla käytössään merkkivalmistajan tarjoamat ja ylläpitämät diagnostiikkatyökalut tai valmistajan hyväksymät tai teknisesti vastaavat. Huollot toteutetaan pääsääntöisesti kauden ulkopuolella yleensä touko- syyskuun välisenä ajankohtana. Huolto tapahtuu tilaajan tarjoamissa tiloissa Oulun talousalueella (Kanta Oulu, Haukipudas, Kiiminki, Ylikiiminki ja Yli-Ii). Akuuttikorjauspalvelu tehdään tilaajan tilaamana ennalta arvaamattomien vikatilanteiden osalta. Korjaustyö on akuuttia, välitöntä ja välttämätöntä korjausta, johon tulee reagoida sopimuksen mukaisella kiireellisellä aikataululla. Korjaukset tehdään pääsääntöisesti koneiden käyttöpaikalla maastossa. Huolto- ja korjauspalvelussa hankittavien varaosien tulee olla uusia ja alkuperäislaatuisia. Materiaaleille ja varaosille on voimassa kiinteä kateprosentti, joka on 5%. Alkuperäiset varaosien ostolaskut tulee liittää tilaajalle toimitettavaan laskuun mukaan. Tilaajalla on oikeus tarpeen mukaan tilata erikseen yksittäisiä varaosia ja tarvikkeita palveluntuottajalta omaan kalustoon. Tilaaja voi poistaa / lisätä huolto- ja korjauspalvelun piiriin kuuluvaa kalustoa vuosittain. Tilaaja informoi muutoksista palveluntuottajaa. Mikäli Tilaajalle tulee uusia tarjouspyynnössä mainitsemattomia laitemerkkejä, voi tilaaja pyytää puitesopimuskumppaneilta minikilpailutuksen kautta tarjoushinnat uudelle laitemerkille. Tarjoukset eivät saa sisältää omia ehtoja. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamäärään. Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä kaikki tarjoukset perustellusta syystä. Sopimusehdot JYSE Palvelut 2025

title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 18 November 2026 at 9:00AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses, and to also provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2028 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $37 million Magnitude of Construction: $100 - $500 million Project Title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day. Purpose: The purpose of this scheduled Industry Day is to provide the latest information regarding the future advertisement and award of Contract 1 for the Tampa Harbor Deepening Project. The scheduled event will include a detailed presentation by the Jacksonville District US Army Corps of Engineers, Tampa Harbor Project Delivery Team (PDT) followed by open Q&A and 1-1 meeting opportunities with contracts to ask more in-depth questions and get feedback as the design and permitting moves forward. Project Description: The project includes construction dredging to deepen and widen specified areas within the federal navigation channel of Tampa Harbor. The project is planned for six (6) contracts over an estimated 8�10-year period. The Scope of Work for this Industry Day will be focused on Contract 1. Contract 1 work includes deepening of Cut-C (HB), Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, East Bay Channel and Cut-D (HB) to a depth of 49 feet MLLW, deepening the Port Sutton Terminal Channel to a depth of 44 feet MLLW, and deepening the East Bay Channel Extensions 1 and 2 to a depth of 41 feet MLLW. The Contract 1 work also includes widening of Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, and East Bay Channel. All areas of deepening and widening will incorporate +1 foot of allowable overdepth. All dredged material from the project will be disposed of in the East Bay Placement Area, DMMA 2-D and DMMA 3-D. Estimated quantities to be dredged are roughly 4.4 million cubic yards. Link to the Tampa Harbor Improvements USACE website: https://www.saj.usace.army.mil/Tampa-Harbor/-30-/ Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: 1. Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. 2. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? 3. Describe the proposed construction methods and sequencing and equipment needed to complete the project. At a minimum, address pre-dredging, side-casting of pre-dredging material, and placement into the East Bay Placement Area including constructing the containment perimeter and filling within the area. The contract will include geologic data of the dredge and placement areas as well as the geotechnical requirements for materials considered suitable for constructing the containment perimeter. The contractor will propose the dredging sequence to accomplish constructing the containment perimeter that meets required geotechnical specifications. Describe the factors considered in determining the dredging sequence, such as the material type, proposed equipment, proximity to the placement area, etc.? 4. Describe any constructability, stability, safety concerns with East Bay Placement Area. Describe additional equipment or methods required to place infill above water and/or above the proposed crest of the containment perimeter. Describe any concerns for drainage of the placement area. 5. Describe how filling the East Bay Placement Area will not result in material migrating out of the placement area and into the federal channel. At a minimum, address how existing soft material at the placement area will be contained when disturbed. 6. Will the proposed East Bay Placement Area construction methods require equipment to be located within the federal channel for extended periods of time acting as obstructions for vessel traffic, or obstruct Port Tampa Bay Berth 150? 7. For East Bay Placement Area, describe any temporal facilities, staging and laydown areas, and utilities that would be required or preferred in adjacent upland areas. 8. Dredging and placement of material will be conducted in a manner to minimize turbidity. Describe the turbidity control measures, such as turbidity curtains, that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If hydraulic placement of infill is proposed for the East Bay Placement Area, describe how affluent will be managed. 9. Based on prior dredging construction experience either in Tampa Bay or other locations in Florida, what are some of the challenges USACE could streamline to improve contract execution? 10. Describe any concerns with execution of the environmental species monitoring and reporting. Event Date: Wednesday, 18 November 2026 at 9:00 AM EST. Event Location: Port of Tampa � Cruise Terminal 6 1331 McKay Street Tampa, Florida 33602 *Parking available onsite For more information, please see the Industry Day Agenda copy under the Attachments. Contact Info: Manny Vianzon, Project Manager (904) 232-3292 Emmanuel.A.Vianzon@usace.army.mil If you cannot attend in person: Link Meeting: https://www.microsoft.com/EN-US/MICROSOFT-TEAMS/JOIN-A-MEETING Meeting ID: 993 212 869 457 Passcode: tG6Ff3Gt Join by phone: 604-262-2433 Phone conference ID: 972 118 411# NOTES: NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COST ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO SAID NOTICE, ATTENDANCE AT THE VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY EVENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION SUBSEQUENTLY REQUESTED. You must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to receive a Government contract award. To register, go to www.sam.gov. For additional information visit the website for the Federal Service Desk (www.FSD.gov) which supports SAM or contact them at 866-606-8220 for assistance.

title: Q&A for Third Party Liability (TPL) Insurance for All Embassy Vehicles (OFV)
description: 1.Could you please confirm whether the semiannual insurance premiums are payable in advance upon policy issuance and acceptance, or after completion of each six-month coverage period? Answer: The Government will award this solicitation as an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract. In line with local government policy, the Government will pay the full third-party liability (TPL) insurance premium one year in advance. If the Government adds a vehicle during the year, it will issue a task order, and the TPL insurance for that vehicle will cover only the days left in the policy year. 2. Please clarify whether invoices may be submitted at the beginning of each coverage period and the expected payment timeline following invoice acceptance. Answer: Please refer to Answer 1 3. Share your sponsor Number/computer Number if Commercial Registration is not available. Answer: The Embassy will give the applicable government registration number to the successful offeror at award. Offerors do not need this number to submit a proposal. 4. Fleet Details in Excel Format: Kindly provide an Excel file containing the details of all vehicles to be insured, including the following information for each vehicle: Serial Number Chassis Number (VIN) Vehicle Make and Type Model Year Answer: All of the requested information can be found in the main solicitation, with the exception of the serial numbers. Please see the attached Excel spreadsheet. 5. May a U.S.- registered company serve as the prime contractor while a licensed Saudi insurance company provides the policies, claims management, and legal services? Answer: The policies must be issued by an insurer licensed to underwrite motor insurance in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as Saudi law requires. A non-insurer prime contractor may offer policies issued by a licensed Saudi insurer under a subcontract or teaming arrangement. The proposal must identify the insurer and include its license and Commercial Registration (CR) number. The prime contractor remains fully responsible for performance. 6. Would our previous experience in the UAE managing insurance for a fleet of 55 rental vehicles, together with the experience of a licensed Saudi insurance partner, satisfy the solicitation's past performance requirements? Answer: The Government will evaluate past performance under Section 4 evaluation criteria. The Government may consider the relevant past performance of proposed subcontractors or teaming partners who will perform major parts of the work. Offerors should describe how relevant their past contracts are in scope, size, and complexity. The Government does not decide in advance whether specific experience is acceptable. 7. Does the USD 55,000 contract maximum include VAT and all premiums for the 221 vehicles? Answer: The contract maximum of USD 55,000 all premiums for the 221 vehicles over. The Embassy is exempt from VAT / the Embassy reclaims VAT through the host-government refund program; offerors should price exclusive of VAT and show it as a separate line item. 8. Does Exhibit 1 represent the complete available claims history? If not, can additional loss-run information be provided? Answer: Exhibit 1 � Please find below the complete three years profit and loss ratio. 9. May the licensed Saudi insurance partner perform all claims administration and legal representation obligations on behalf of the prime contractor? Answer: A licensed Saudi insurer or subcontractor may perform claims administration and legal representation. The prime contractor remains fully responsible for meeting all contract obligations. The proposal must identify the entity that will perform these services.

title: Preventive Maintenance Service for One (1) Oxford Nanoimaging ONI Nanoimager
description: Title Preventive Maintenance Service for One (1) Oxford Nanoimaging ONI Nanoimager Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute (NCI), intends to award a contract to Oxford Nanoimaging Inc on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of Annual Service Plan - Nanoimager, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements will be satisfied by Oxford Nanoimaging Inc. Tumor cells, immune cells, and irradiated tissues release large quantities of biologically active nanoscale extracellular vesicles (EVs). The Translational Nanobiology Section within the Laboratory of Pathology (LP) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute (NCI), Center for Cancer Research (CCR), is developing new ways to investigate these EVs as biological agents, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets. The section uses an Oxford Nanoimaging (ONI) Nanoimager super-resolution microscope to provide high quality singlemolecule resolution imaging for nanoparticle analysis as part of the section�s EV production and analysis pipeline. Preventive maintenance services are required to ensure its highest peak performance, as this instrument is being used for developing guidelines for best practices in this area of research, and ultimately for establishing a foundation for next-generation EV-based personalized cancer treatment and monitoring. This acquisition is to acquire preventive maintenance services for a super resolution microscope system, Oxford Nanoimaging (ONI) Nanoimager, at the Laboratory of Pathology. Oxford Nanoimaging Inc (ONI) is the original manufacturer and sole provider of authorized maintenance services for the ONI Nanoimager super-resolution microscope. Due to the sensitive nature of the superresolution microscope, it can only be repaired by qualified, OEM-trained technicians. This specialized training is only accessible to Oxford Nanoimaging technicians. Furthermore, only Oxford Nanoimaging can provide access to genuine, proprietary OEM spare parts which are required to maintain this superresolution microscope. The OEM does not license 3rd party technicians, and spare or replacement parts for this instrument can only be obtained from the original manufacturer. Thus, no other vendor has trained personnel to work with this complex system or access to any potential required parts that might need replacing over time. Lastly, the operating system and software of this super-resolution microscope are proprietary and can only be serviced by Oxford Nanoimaging. All updates and patches are solely available through the OEM This makes Oxford Nanoimaging the only known source for this requirement and the only provider that can meet the Government�s needs at this time. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 18, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00010 in the subject line of the response

title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation or via amendment. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend.

title: Whistlers Campground Shower Replacement - Jasper National Park
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to bid solicitations is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) has a requirement for the demolition, removal, and replacement of existing Corian wall and floor systems in seasonal campground washrooms at Whistlers Campground, Jasper National Park To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $500,001 > $1,000,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI03 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor shall perform and complete the Work no later than March 26, 2027. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

description: The IF109 Framework is being established to support delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme and will succeed the existing IF105 Integrated Partnerships Framework, which is due to expire in May 2028. The Framework is intended to support delivery of the PC28 investment programme and future regulatory periods whilst securing the capacity, capability, flexibility, value for money and resilience required to deliver NI Water's future capital programme. The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework will support a range of works and related services including programme and project management, design, engineering, construction, commissioning and other supporting or ancillary activities necessary to support the successful delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme. The Framework is intended to support delivery of NI Water's future investment priorities, including regulatory compliance, service improvement, resilience enhancement, environmental performance and long-term sustainability objectives. The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework comprises four Lots covering: Lot 1 - Minor Civil Pipelaying Works Lot 2 - Minor Civil Works Lot 3 - Minor MEICA & Process Works Lot 4 - Major Civil, MEICA & Process Works Together, these Lots will support the delivery of projects ranging from small-scale network investment and rehabilitation activities through to large-scale, complex, multidisciplinary capital programmes across NI Water's water and wastewater asset base. The Framework has been designed to support long-term delivery of NI Water's investment programme whilst providing the flexibility required to respond to evolving programme, funding and operational requirements throughout its duration. The total framework value may be shared across all Lots.

title: Additional Bloomberg Shared Terminals for CFTC
description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) intends to increase the value of its existing contract with Bloomberg Financial L.P on a sole-source basis for three (3) additional Bloomberg professional terminals. The anticipated modification will increase the value of each of the remaining four annual contract periods. The ultimate expiration date of the contract is June 30, 2030. CFTC uses a variety of information sources to maintain surveillance of commodity market activity. There is no single source that provides all the information that CFTC needs for market oversight. Bloomberg is one of those sources and is a unique source for its proprietary financial data. Additionally, Bloomberg is the only vendor that offers a shared terminal service (as opposed to individual licenses). The Government intends to procure this requirement under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 6.103-1 and 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) because �the property or services needed by the executive agency are available from only one responsible source and no other type of property or services will satisfy the needs of the executive agency.� THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS nor a solicitation of offers. However, the Government will consider written responses from all responsible sources received by 10:00 AM ET, November 18, 2026. Written responses must include sufficient information to establish capability to fulfill the requirement. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purposes for future Market Research requirements. No formal solicitation package is available. The Government anticipates award on or about November 30, 2026. The Government will not be responsible for any costs of preparation in response to this announcement.

title: USCGC MORRO BAY (WTGB-108) � Fuel Oil Tanks and Bilge Cleaning and Inspection
description: The U.S. Coast Guard has a requirement for a qualified contractor to furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, vacuum trucks, and hoses to perform fuel oil tank and bilge cleaning services aboard the USCGC MORRO BAY (WTGB-108) in Cleveland, OH. Bilge Cleaning: Vacuum offload approximately 2,500 gallons of mixed fluid (used engine oil, fuel, and bilge water). Thoroughly wash and degrease bilges to meet USCG-provided Marine Chemist gas-free/safe-for-hot-work inspection standards. Fuel Oil (F/O) Tank Cleaning & Fuel Disposal: Pump low-suction residue and dispose of approximately 11,500 gallons of contaminated Marine Gas Oil (MGO) / diesel fuel. Clean all internal tank surfaces free of residual fuel, sludge, biological growth, and foreign matter. Continuous media extraction and lint-free wipe-down required (per drawings 140 WTGB 116-001, 140-003, 120-001, and 149-001). Tank Inspection & Closure: Verify Tank Level Indicator (TLI) system operation and removal of all pipe plugs prior to entry and closure. Secure manhole covers in the presence of the Coast Guard Inspector using new AMS-C-6183 compliant gaskets, chasing stud threads, and renewing damaged nuts. Environmental & Waste Documentation: Provide full chain-of-custody documentation and signed Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest(s) within two (2) calendar days of work completion. 2. Period & Place of Performance Location: USCGC MORRO BAY, 1055 East 9th Street, Cleveland, OH 44114. Performance Window: 20 November 2026 through 01 December 2026. Preferred Start: 20 November 2026 at 08:30 EST. On-Site Cap: Not to exceed three (3) consecutive calendar days. Holiday: Thanksgiving Day (26 November 2026) is an official non-work day. 3. Mandatory Contractor Qualifications & Equipment Offerors must demonstrate and provide proof of the following with their quote: Vacuum truck operators certified for over-the-water oil transfer. Capability to provide an operational vacuum truck and a minimum of 200 feet of suction hose. Valid federal/state waste transporter credentials and permitted destination facility details. Personnel must hold valid government-issued photo ID (REAL ID or TWIC) for base entry. Note: The Government will supply the Marine Chemist only. All other tools, rigging, parts, and consumables are contractor-furnished. 5. Site Visit Date & Time: 19 November 2026, 08:00 � 13:00 EST. *IN THE SOW IT STATES: 17NOV2026 THIS IS INCORRECT Location: USCGC MORRO BAY, 1055 East 9th Street, Cleveland, OH 44114. Registration: Site visit coordination must be made at least 24 hours in advance with the Ship's Representative: CWO Gregory Tarker, (206) 815-6706, gregory.e.tarker@uscg.mil. 6. Submission Instructions & Evaluation Quote Package: Submit via email to KS Justin Wooldridge and justin.r.woolridge2@uscg.mil by the response deadline. Must include: Technical proof of over-the-water transfer certifications and 200 ft hose/equipment availability. Company CAGE code, UEI, and point of contact details. Evaluation: Award will be made on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis to a responsible offeror registered in SAM.gov meeting all mandatory technical specifications and schedule requirements.

title: 6515--Pearson Neuropsych testing supplies
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, intends to negotiate a sole-source contract with Pearson Clinical Assessment/Pearson Education, Inc. for the purchase of Pearson neuropsychological testing instruments, assessment kits, consumables, manuals, stimulus materials, and Q-global digital scoring and reporting products for the Durham VA Health Care System (VAHCS) Neuropsychology program. The requirement is for Pearson neuropsychological assessment kits, instruments, consumables, manuals, stimulus materials, and related Q-global digital scoring and reporting products. These supplies support the evaluation of Veterans with cognitive deficits, including dementia and cognitive residuals associated with traumatic brain injury, and will support expanded neuropsychological testing capacity at the Garner Health Care Center. Pearson products are required to ensure compatibility among the standardized assessment instruments, current editions and forms, administration and scoring materials, and Q-global digital scoring and reporting platform. The contractor shall provide new, complete, current products in the specified editions, formats, quantities, and subscription terms identified in the Government item schedule. No clinical services are being procured under this requirement. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. No solicitation documents are available, and telephone requests will not be accepted. However, any business that believes it can meet these requirements and possesses the relevant products, experience, and expertise may submit written notice of its capability. Supporting documentation must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the firm s ability to provide the required Pearson-compatible assessment instruments, consumables, manuals, stimulus materials, Q-global subscriptions, digital scoring products, and reports in the required editions, formats, quantities, and subscription terms. Responses will be considered by the Government; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses must identify the business size status, authorized distribution or reseller status where applicable, relevant past experience, and the specific products offered. Brand-name-or-equal products must meet all applicable salient physical, functional, and performance characteristics established by the Government. The applicable NAICS code is 334516 Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a size standard of 1,000 employees. Responses received by 10am EST. on November 18th, 2026, will be considered by the Government. Responses and inquiries may be emailed to Ricardo.McIntosh@va.gov. No telephone requests will be accepted.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL QUALIFICATION TESTING (EQT)
description: N00164-27-S-NC12 - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT � ENVIRONMENTAL QUALIFICATION TESTING (EQT) - PSC H270 - NAICS 541380 Issue Date: 29 OCT 2026 - Closing Date: 18 NOV 2026 - 11:00 AM EST REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - The Government is issuing this RFI/sources sought announcement as part of market research for usage of Environmental Qualification Testing (EQT). The objective is to engage a qualified testing contractor to perform environmental qualification testing (EQT) to verify that this updated enclosure assembly and workstation mount meets all naval shipboard survival and operational requirements. The Statement of Work (SOW) defines the requirements for environmental and electromagnetic compatibility testing of the Combined All-Domain Command and Control System Afloat (CAC2S Afloat) Data Processing Assembly and Workstation Mount. See attached SOW to review the technical requirements provided as Attachment 1 to this document. Vendors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and registered in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive access to the SOW. Information about the JCP is located at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/. In accordance with Department of Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Procedures, Guidance, and Information (PGI) 206.302-1, the Government is accepting information from companies potentially capable of meeting the requirements as described above. Companies with the capabilities and facilities to provide this testing that meets the Government�s requirements and certification requirements may respond. Responses shall address requirements as discussed within the SOW. All interested parties may submit company and product literature, a white paper no longer than 5 pages, and/or other pertinent information, such as a description with performance parameters and a statement of current availability, summary of prior testing, test reports, a budgetary estimate, and an explanation as to why the Government should not procure this effort on a sole source basis as stated above given the requirements set forth. Responses to the Market Survey shall include the following: Submitter�s Name Street Address, City, State, Zip Code Business Size Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone Announcement Number: N00164-27-S-NC12 Please include the purpose/explanation of the response to the Market Survey, i.e. to better understand the Government requirements; to potentially become a viable source for future requirements; to take exception to the anticipated sole source as your company currently meets all of the Government requirements. The Government may contact RFI respondents to get clarification on the information submitted. Submissions may be sent by any government or non- governmental entity including commercial firms, non-profit organizations, and institutions of higher education with degree-granting programs in science and/or engineering (universities), or by consortia comprising such concerns. Responses from Small and Small Disadvantaged Business firms are highly encouraged. Firms responding should indicate if they are a small business, a socially and economically disadvantaged business, 8(a) firms, historically black colleges or universities, and minority institutions. Contractors must be properly registered in the Government's System for Award Management (SAM) and in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive the attachments. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.sam.gov. Information about on JCP is located at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/. At the current time, NO FUNDING IS AVAILABLE for contractual efforts. This RFI/sources sought does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The US Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Market Survey information may be submitted to the Point of Contact (POC) any time prior to the expiration of this announcement. The POC for this effort is Ms. Morgan Helton, morgan.m.helton.civ@us.navy.mil Responses to this RFI/sources sought may be emailed to the POC above. If any part of the submittal is classified, please contact the POC for appropriate submission information. title: CGC CALHOUN MAKO Breathing Air compressor parts
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price supply contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. This requirement consists of providing MAKO Breathing Air Compressor Service Parts in support of SCBA bottle refilling capability aboard CGC CALHOUN. Do not list individual line items, quantities, part numbers, National Stock Numbers, or technical specifications in this notice. The complete itemized requirement, including quantities, part numbers, and specifications, is contained in the attached Statement of Work and associated line-item schedule. All items must be delivered on an F.O.B. Destination basis to North Charleston, South Carolina by 22-JAN-2027. This acquisition is unrestricted under NAICS code 333912, with a corresponding small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The applicable Product Service Code is 4310. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation is most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) 2. Past Performance (Pass/Fail) 3. Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the supplies, including but not limited to manufacturing, packaging, handling, transportation, duties, tariffs, fees, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. title: Equipment: Lonza 4D-Nucleofector� System
description: 1. Disclaimer THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and market research planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB), nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. No contract or purchase order will be awarded from this announcement, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing a response. 2. Background and Purpose The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions,, Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD), Section of Cell Cycle Regulation, has a requirement for a Brand-Name Lonza 4D-Nucleofector� System consisting of the following: 4D-Nucleofector Core Unit, Part No. AAF-1003B � Quantity (1) EA 4D-Nucleofector X Unit, Part No. AAF-1003X - Quantity (1) EA 3. One-year warranty extension for each unit. Or a functional domestic equivalent, to support ongoing NIH-funded research involving the genetic manipulation of mammalian cells. Because NICHD's ongoing studies rely on previously validated electroporation pulse-code workflows, experimental protocols, and Nucleocuvette� consumables established on a prior-generation Lonza Nucleofector platform, the Lonza 4D-Nucleofector� System is the primary known platform capable of ensuring experimental reproducibility and data continuity without requiring costly and time-consuming protocol re-optimization or re-validation. The Office of Acquisitions is conducting market research to identify qualified vendors�including small businesses, authorized distributors, and domestic manufacturers�and specifically seeks market information to determine: 1. Authorized Lonza Sources: The availability of Lonza Walkersville, Inc. or authorized distributors/resellers (including small businesses, HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, and Small Disadvantaged Businesses under NAICS 334516) capable of supplying new Lonza equipment with full manufacturer-backed warranties. 2. Buy American Act (FAR Part 25) Compliance: The availability of any domestic end products manufactured in the United States capable of meeting all functional, warranty, training, and legacy workflow-continuity requirements outlined in Section 3 without requiring experimental re-validation. 3. Technical Requirements and Salient Characteristics To meet the Government's minimum requirements, the proposed system must satisfy all functional and technical specifications from the Statement of Work alongside the laboratory's workflow-continuity constraints: Core Control Unit: The system shall include a Lonza 4D-Nucleofector� Core Unit (or a domestic equivalent central control unit) capable of controlling and operating advanced electroporation-based transfection protocols. Small-Volume Transfection Module: The system shall include a Lonza 4D-Nucleofector� X Unit (or a domestic equivalent functional module) capable of processing small-volume samples (specifically ranging from 20 �L to 100 �L) and supporting transfection of primary cells and other difficult-to-transfect cell types. Nucleic Acid & Reagent Delivery: The system shall support delivery of plasmid DNA, RNA, siRNA, CRISPR/Cas9 reagents, and other nucleic acid-based materials into mammalian cells. Optimized Transfection Performance: The system shall provide optimized electroporation programs designed to maximize transfection efficiency while maintaining high post-transfection cell viability. Sensitive Cell Applications: The system shall support research applications involving primary cells, stem cells, immune cells, and other sensitive cell populations that are not efficiently transfected using conventional lipid-based methods. Software and Protocols: The system shall include manufacturer-provided software and protocols necessary for operation of the instrument. Warranty Coverage: The system shall include a minimum one-year manufacturer warranty and one-year warranty extension coverage for both the Core Unit and X Unit (two years total coverage). Warranty coverage shall begin upon Government acceptance of the equipment and continue in accordance with the manufacturer's warranty terms. Consumable & Legacy Protocol Continuity: If proposing Lonza equipment, the system shall be 100% compatible with commercially available Lonza Nucleofector� reagents, Nucleocuvette� consumables, and existing pulse-code workflows previously developed and validated on a prior-generation Lonza Nucleofector platform. If proposing a domestic alternative, the vendor must demonstrate that its system and consumables achieve equivalent transfection efficiency and post-transfection cell viability across NICHD's existing mammalian cell workflows without requiring protocol re-optimization or experimental re-validation. Delivery, Installation, and Training: Equipment must be delivered to NIH Bethesda (Building 49) and installed, with on-site or virtual user training for up to five (5) NIH personnel completed within 30 days of installation (covering system operation, software functionality, routine maintenance, and basic troubleshooting). All delivery, installation, and training shall be completed within the 12-month period of performance from award. 4. Capability Statement Submission Instructions Interested organizations that believe they can meet all requirements outlined in Section 3 are invited to submit a tailored Capability Statement (no more than 5 pages) containing the following information: 1. Company Profile: Organization name, mailing address, primary Point of Contact (name, title, email, and telephone number), SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (UEI), and CAGE code. 2. Business Size & Socioeconomic Status: Business size under NAICS 334516 (1,000-employee size standard) and applicable socioeconomic designations (e.g., Small Business, Woman-Owned, Veteran-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone, 8(a)). 3. Contract Vehicles: Identification of any existing federal contract vehicles held by the vendor through which this equipment can be ordered (e.g., GSA Multiple Award Schedule), or confirmation of open-market availability. 4. Country of Origin (COO): Explicit identification of the manufacturing country of origin for all proposed hardware components and confirmation of whether the system qualifies as a domestic end product under the Buy American Act (FAR Part 25). 5. Technical Capability & Authorization: Product brochures, technical specifications, and catalog numbers demonstrating compliance with every requirement in Section 3. If proposing Lonza equipment: Documentation confirming status as an Authorized Distributor/Reseller eligible to provide new equipment and manufacturer-backed warranties. If proposing a domestic alternative: Technical evidence proving equivalent transfection performance and workflow continuity with existing NICHD mammalian cell protocols without requiring experimental re-validation. 6. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Pricing (Optional): Non-binding budgetary pricing estimate for market research purposes. 5. Place of Performance: NIH, 9000 Rockville Pike, Bethesda, MD 20892 6. Submission Deadline and Contact Information Please submit electronic Capability Statements in PDF or Microsoft Word format via email to Tina Robinson at robinsti@mail.nih.gov no later than November 18, 2026, at 11:00 AM EST. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Capability Statements must reference Notice Number 75N98027R00019. Email submissions and any questions must be sent to robinsti@mail.nih.gov and include Notice Number 75N98027R00019 in the subject line. Capability Statements and attachments will not be returned to the sender. This synopsis is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for information solicited.

description: AMENDMENT 02 (09/21/2026): The purpose of this amendment is to incorporate PHMSA�s Responses to Vendor Inquiries regarding Phase I white paper submissions, subcontractor eligibility for foreign entities, submission limits, deadlines, and multi-topic proposals under the solicitation (See attached). All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- AMENDMENT 01 (08/24/2026): The purpose of this amendment is to (1) change the Phase I White Paper due date from December 22, 2026, to November 18, 2026, and (2) add the contact email address tremayne.terry@dot.gov to Section X.A. in Attachment 1- BAA Solicitation_PHMSA-26HM-BAA. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. Full eligibility, formatting, and submission instructions are detailed in the solicitation document attached to this notice.

All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. Full eligibility, formatting, and submission instructions are detailed in the solicitation document attached to this notice.
